purpose: Every quantitative claim in the published documentation that could change a researcher's methodological choices, with the evidence and the method needed to recompute it. Read by replicate.py, which ships with the distribution so a recipient can challenge these without reconstructing the extraction pipeline.

kinds.measurement: Recomputable from the distribution by independent code. A discrepancy is a defect in the claim or the data.
kinds.estimate: Recomputable only under a stated assumption. A discrepancy may mean the assumption differs, not that either side is wrong. The assumption is named in `assumes`.
kinds.interpretation: A statement about what a field MEANS or what a measurement licenses. Not mechanically checkable, recorded so a reader knows which claims rest on judgement rather than arithmetic.

cross_representation: `independent_of` names the published representation the claim's own figure came from. Where the replication reads a DIFFERENT representation the check is genuinely independent; where it reads the same one, `same_representation: true` says so, because two calculations over one extraction can agree while both are wrong.

claims.description: Span of the primary (hardware timer) row duration across all tracks
Tracks whose hardware row is coarser than the 10 ms uniform row
Note attacks carrying a recovered pitch
Note-on events in the published MIDI tree
claims.reads: midi/*.mid, parsed as a Standard MIDI File byte stream
claims.note: The strongest cross-representation check available: a binary format produced by a different code path from the JSON tables, parsed here without reference to either.

claims.description: Largest number of voices sounding at once anywhere in the corpus
claims.reads: events/*.json.gz, interval sweep with the documented 1 us remedy
claims.note: Exercises the documented rounding remedy. Without it a naive sweep reports 9-13, which is the defect the remedy exists for.

claims.documented_in: DATASET.md, Pitch is usable in bulk
claims.independent_of: none published; this figure exists only in prose

claims.description: Games whose gated-voice measure is saturated (duty cycle >= 0.95)
claims.reads: events/*.json.gz, recomputing duty from note intervals
claims.independent_of: performance_music.json voices.gated_duty_cycle, which is computed from the extraction records rather than from the published events
claims.note: The claim this checks was wrong in rc6: the prose named two games where the field flags three.

claims.description: timbre_class is the constant -1 wherever it appears
Onsets concentrate far more on onset_grid than on the timer clock (ordering and a gap of at least 0.3)
claims.reads: events/*.json.gz onsets against scores/*.json.gz onset_grid and clock
claims.assumes: circular resultant length of onset phase within the period. The VALUE is estimator-dependent -- an independent estimator gave 0.779/0.344 against the documented 0.937/0.262 -- so the registered claim is the ordering and the size of the gap, which any reasonable estimator should reproduce.

claims.description: Median per-sample deviation from an exact semitone ladder, worst driver
claims.assumes: free offset fitted per sample group by scanning in 0.01-semitone steps, over groups of at least 8 pitched attacks, then a median per group aggregated PER DRIVER -- a driver pools its games. Aggregating per GAME instead gives 4.06 (Mega Man X), and the first replication failed purely on that unstated choice. Both figures are now registered.

claims.description: A gated voice is not an audible voice; gated concurrency partly measures driver gating habit rather than musical density
claims.not_checkable_because: Deciding when a voice became inaudible needs ADSR release rates, which are not published. The supporting measurements (release gap, duty cycle, the 0.703 correlation) are registered separately or published as fields; the inference from them is judgement.

claims.description: sample_id identifies decoded audio content, not an instrument or a musical role
claims.not_checkable_because: A definitional claim about what the identifier denotes. The corpus can show that one sample is used across a wide pitch span, which is evidence that the distinction matters, but cannot establish the definition.

units_of_analysis.note: The statistical unit a figure is computed over. Published per claim because pooling over tracks lets one game dominate: Earthbound is 13.8% of music tracks and games range from 17 to 139 tracks, an 8x spread. A per-track pooled mean is a mean over a sample weighted by how many tracks each game happens to contribute, which is an artefact of what was collected.
units_of_analysis.track: every track contributes equally; large games dominate
units_of_analysis.game: every game contributes equally; the usual choice for a cross-game claim
units_of_analysis.composer: credits are MANY-TO-MANY and some are truncated at 32 characters: Earthbound's three credited composers each appear on all 139 of its tracks, so a composer-pooled figure multiply-counts those tracks

generalisation.note: Whether a figure describes this corpus or SNES music. NO corpus-wide figure here generalises: 22 games of roughly 700 commercial SNES titles, JRPG- and first-party-weighted, 13.8% from one game. A corpus-wide statistic is descriptive of the collected sample and is not a universal SNES musical convention.
generalisation.sample_composition: 22 games, 1,006 music tracks, 37 credited composers; largest game 13.8%, top three games 28.5%, top three composers 27.4% of credits

populations.note: The sampling frame a claim describes. A SELECTION RULE, not a size: the rule is stable across releases and the realised size is not, so replicate.py reports the size it finds and a report from a 22-game release can be compared with one from a 50-game release rule by rule. `generalises_beyond_corpus: false` says a claim does not describe SNES music; this says which subset of the corpus it does describe. Those are different statements, and several distinct populations exist inside one corpus.

all_indexed_tracks.rule: every track in index.json, any track_class

game_weighted_music.rule: music tracks aggregated per game, each game contributing equally

all_published_events.rule: every row of every events table, both origins

midi_files.rule: the published midi/*.mid files, one per track with a pitched note

dense_sample_groups.rule: (game_slug, sample_id) groups with at least 8 pitched attacks

sampled_tracks.rule: a deterministic spread of tracks, used where an exhaustive pass would cost more than the claim is worth

measured_on_note: Each claim's `reported` figure was measured on the data release named in its `measured_on` block. A claim is NOT APPLICABLE to a release with a different population: recomputing a 22-game figure over 27 games and calling the difference a defect is a sampling-frame error, not a replication failure.
